purpose: Resolves 'which canon styles which screen'. Two tiers — operator vs product — so SOCC's canonical style is used EVERYWHERE it belongs (operator surfaces), and never bleeds onto customer surfaces (which would kill sales).

tier_1_operator_surfaces.canon: SOCC_DESIGN_CANON_V1 (matrix-minimalism: bg #0B0F14, cyan #22D3EE, mono, header box, badges, state dots)
tier_1_operator_surfaces.rule: ALWAYS render through SOCC canon. This is your cockpit. One style, everywhere here.

tier_2_product_surfaces.canon: the ENTITY's own brand canon (ANNA_DESIGN_CANON = D3; Марк = copper; etc.)
tier_2_product_surfaces.rule: render through the PRODUCT's brand. The matrix/SOCC look must NEVER appear to a customer.

what_every_tier_shares: VOICE-law from SOCC canon (calm, precise, honest, no hype, no fake PASS)
PROOF discipline (truth_boundary, REVIEW vs SEALED, gates)
design-TOKEN structure (same token shape, different values per brand)
what_differs: the PALETTE + type skin + mark — operator = matrix; each product = its own warm brand
why_you_didnt_see_socc_style: Operator views were emitted as JSON panels (data) but rarely RENDERED into a SOCC-canon screen; product views were (correctly) in ANNA's warm brand. Fix = a single SOCC-canon control room that renders the whole Forge.
truth_boundary: Surface law only. Declares operator-vs-product canon assignment for all SOCC surfaces. Renders nothing by itself; the control room is the operator-tier render.
